title: Associate Director, Tech Delivery & Service Management
description:
About the Team:

Enterprise Systems is the backbone of GSK’s internal operations in Digital & Tech, enabling GSK Global Functions teams such as Finance, Procurement, HR, Legal, Compliance, WREF, CGA and Corporate Secretariat to run seamlessly. This team designs and delivers cutting-edge digital platforms that power critical processes, ensuring efficiency, compliance, and scalability across the enterprise.

Enterprise Systems Management & Business Operations delivers digital solutions that support Enterprise Systems running as a high-performing organisation. This team drives financial discipline, operational rigour and strategic alignment across the ES portfolio that safeguard GSK’s integrity and reputation globally. By joining this team, you’ll help shape systems that support thousands of employees worldwide, driving innovation and reliability in the tools that keep GSK moving forward.

Job Purpose:

· The Associate Director, Tech Delivery & Service Management is accountable for integrated delivery governance, service transition and operational acceptance across GSK’s External Manufacturing and Digital Pack portfolio. The role takes approved product, programmer and solution outcomes through coordinated delivery, deployment, handover and early-life support into stable, supportable and compliant live services. It ensures delivery and operational risks are actively managed across business-critical processes connecting GSK, contract manufacturing organizations, packaging partners and Digital Pack teams.

· The role connects Product teams, architects, External Manufacturing and Digital Pack stakeholders, service functions, Finance and strategic partners. It establishes one integrated view of approved priorities, milestones, dependencies, capacity, funding, forecasts, risks and decisions, and coordinates delivery and service-readiness dependencies across product supply, partner onboarding, packaging, artwork, labelling, pack data, quality, enterprise platforms and external partners. The role does not own the External Manufacturing technology strategy, product or solution roadmap, business case, solution direction or end-to-end transformation value realization; these remain with the accountable Product or Technology lead.

· The role supports resilient operations, effective partner collaboration and simpler operations through standardization, automation and responsible use of AI. It maintains security, quality, Gapp and regulatory controls where applicable, with clear human accountability for decisions affecting product quality, continuity of supply and regulated packaging, artwork and labelling processes.

Key Responsibilities:

· Own the coordinated transition of approved new and changed technology capabilities into stable, supportable and compliant live services for assigned External Manufacturing and Digital Pack products, services and cross-functional initiatives, from integrated delivery planning through deployment, handover and early-life support. Accountable Product and Technology leads retain ownership of strategy, roadmap, scope, solution direction, adoption outcomes and value realisation.

· Own integrated delivery governance for the portfolio through agreed plans, governance forums and decision controls covering approved priorities, milestones, entry and exit criteria, critical paths, dependencies, capacity, resources, risks, issues and decisions across business teams, GSK technology groups, contract manufacturers, packaging partners and strategic suppliers. The accountable Product or Technology lead retains accountability for External Manufacturing strategy, transformation priorities and end-to-end programme outcomes.

· Provide service leadership for portfolio products and integrations, ensuring stability, availability, continuity, performance and effective support for manufacturing, packaging, artwork, labelling and pack-data operations.

· Act as the senior escalation point for delivery and operational issues, coordinating rapid recovery and clear decisions where incidents or delays could affect product supply, manufacturing partners, packaging operations or market launch readiness.

· Govern incident, problem, change, configuration and release activities, ensuring root causes are addressed and recurring issues across applications, data flows and business-to-business integrations are prevented.

· Own service transition and operational acceptance for approved new capabilities and major changes, including validated controls, support models, monitoring, runbooks, continuity arrangements, partner onboarding, cutover plans, acceptance evidence and escalation paths before go-live. The accountable Product or Technology lead retains ownership of business readiness, adoption and value outcomes.

· Own portfolio financial governance, including annual planning, budget and forecast management, actuals tracking, resource and supplier cost oversight, variance analysis, financial risks and corrective actions, ensuring investment remains aligned to agreed priorities and outcomes.

· Own benefits baselining and tracking governance across the portfolio. Agree documented baselines, measurable targets, data sources, review dates and a named accountable owner for each benefit with Product and Technology leads, business stakeholders and Finance before implementation. Track actual outcomes against baselines beyond initiative closure against the agreed measurement schedule, validate evidence with benefit owners and Finance, and escalate shortfalls with corrective actions. Feed measured results back into portfolio prioritisation. Accountable Product and Technology leads retain ownership of end-to-end value realisation.

· Maintain portfolio governance dashboards and decision materials covering delivery status, financial performance, service health, benefits, capacity, dependencies, technical debt, partner performance, risks, issues and decisions required. Provide clear recommendations and escalate variances promptly to accountable leaders.

· Partner with stakeholders to prioritise portfolio investments and delivery, resilience, obsolescence, compliance, data quality and integration risks within product and technology roadmaps. Manage technology suppliers and managed service partners against delivery commitments, contractual obligations, costs and service outcomes, retaining GSK accountability for critical and regulated decisions.

· Coach and mentor Tech Delivery and Service staff through practical guidance, knowledge sharing and structured development support. Coach Product Owners and delivery leads on integrated planning, RAID (risks, assumptions, issues and dependencies) and operational readiness to strengthen delivery discipline at source. Build capability in financial and benefits governance, service transition and operational management. Own, maintain and continuously improve delivery and service standards, methods, controls and reusable practices across the portfolio, ensuring consistent adoption and measurable improvement.

· Lead continuous improvement through simplification, standardisation and automation, and use approved AI tools in the role’s own day-to-day work, including AI-assisted reporting, incident analysis and documentation. Check outputs for accuracy, evidence, confidentiality and compliance, retaining human accountability for decisions and final deliverables.

Basic Requirements:

Education & Professional Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Technology, Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Business or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

Area of Specialization

· Program management of technology programs across complex business domains

· Technology delivery and service management of complex products

· Business and Digital products knowledge supporting External Manufacturing and digital pack (Serialization, Artwork and ePI)

· Integrated planning, RAID, dependency and operational-readiness management

· GxP, quality, security and regulatory controls for technology-enabled solutions

· Strategic-partner management

· Automation, AI-enabled operations and continuous improvement

Minimum Level of Job-Related Experience Required

· Typically 7+ years of experience across technology delivery, service management, platform operations or programme/project management in complex global environments.

· Demonstrated experience delivering significant technology change while maintaining stable live services for supply chain, manufacturing, packaging, artwork, labelling or partner-facing operations.

· Strong experience leading portfolio delivery governance, including integrated planning, prioritisation, capacity and dependency management, governance forums, RAID control, executive reporting and decision tracking across multiple products and initiatives.

· Demonstrated expertise in service transition, ITSM practices, operational acceptance, major-incident leadership, root-cause investigation and sustainable remediation.

· Experience defining operational-readiness controls, service models, runbooks, monitoring, continuity, support arrangements and handover criteria.

· Experience working across Product, Engineering, Architecture, Quality and business teams in Agile and/or DevOps environments.

Preferred:

· Relevant certifications in ITIL, programme/project delivery, Agile/Scrum, DevOps or service management are desirable.

· Experience managing contract manufacturers, packaging partners, artwork and labelling service providers, strategic technology partners or outsourced delivery and service arrangements is desirable.

· Experience in a regulated life-sciences environment, including GxP, audit readiness and validated systems, is highly desirable.

Location

Reports To

The Food Services Coordinator reports to the Food Services Supervisor.


Employment Type

This is a full-time, non-exempt role.


Responsibilities

  • Work with Food Service Supervisor to improve existing menu items, and develop a creative and fun dining experience for campers, staff, and volunteers

Benefits

Camp For All offers comprehensive benefits for full-time staff, including 100% employer-paid health, life, and long-term disability coverage. In addition, we provide dental, vision, and supplemental life insurance. Health savings account participants also receive an annual contribution of up to $1,000, broken into bi-weekly payroll contributions.


We are proud to offer generous paid time off, earned every pay period, along with (9) paid holidays and paid paternity leave. Eligible employees can also participate in our 401(k) plan, with an employer matching contribution of up to 4%.

title: AI Engineer
description:
We’re looking for an AI Engineer who enjoys building useful software and wants to do more than experiment with AI, someone who can turn it into reliable solutions that people actually use.

At Boyum IT, we’re exploring how AI can make a real difference across our products and the way we work internally. That might mean building an assistant that helps colleagues find the right information faster, supporting our customer-facing teams with smarter tools, or connecting AI capabilities with our existing products and systems.

This is a practical, hands-on engineering role. You’ll have space to explore new ideas, but the goal is always the same: build something useful, reliable, and ready for the real world.

You don’t need to know every technology in our stack from day one. We’re looking for a strong software engineer who already has some hands-on experience with AI and wants to go deeper.

Location: Aarhus, Denmark - regular office presence is required.

About the Team: We call ourselves the “Unified Platform Services” team and work across products and development teams to build shared solutions and make individual product teams more effective. We also help shape how AI is used across our different products. We are a small team with a mix of skills across AI, DevOps, and traditional software development.

What You Will Be Doing

As our new AI engineer colleague, you will be assigned to specific AI projects and deliveries, but you’ll also share what you learn and help other development teams make effective use of AI tools. As part of these two focus areas, you will:

  • Design, build and maintain AI-powered applications, assistants and services.
  • Develop backend services and APIs.
  • Work with LLM-powered applications, RAG, semantic search and agentic workflows.
  • Build and improve data pipelines and knowledge bases used by AI applications.
  • Help evaluate AI solutions and improve their quality, reliability and accuracy.
  • Deploy and operate solutions in Azure.
  • Work with Docker, CI/CD and Azure DevOps as part of the development lifecycle.
  • Collaborate with product teams and internal functions to understand problems and turn them into practical technical solutions.
  • Build reusable tools, integrations and templates that help other teams work effectively with AI.
  • Share knowledge and contribute to how we use AI across the company.

Our current technology landscape includes Python, PostgreSQL/vector, Dagster, Azure, Azure AI Foundry, MCP, Docker and Azure DevOps.

What We Are Looking For

We think you’ll be a good match if you have:

  • At least 3+ years of software development experience, ideally in backend or software engineering
  • Experience building production services or APIs – ideally AI-related ones
  • Hands-on experience building AI-powered applications or integrating AI into software
  • A solid understanding of databases, testing, and maintainable software
  • Curiosity about where AI genuinely adds value, and where it doesn’t
  • The ability to work with both technical and non-technical colleagues to understand a problem before jumping to a solution

Nice to Have

Experience with any of the following is a bonus, not a checklist:

  • C#
  • Azure or another cloud platform
  • Docker, DevOps, and CI/CD
  • Data pipelines
  • RAG, embeddings, vector databases, or AI agents

Why Join Boyum IT

At Boyum IT, our culture is built around Energy for Life - the belief that people do their best work when they feel energized, supported, and able to balance work with life outside of work.

For us, Energy for Life means creating a workplace where people can grow professionally, stay healthy, feel connected, and have the flexibility to be present for family, friends, and personal priorities.

What We Offer

  • A culture built around our Energy for Life mindset
  • Flexible work arrangements and respect for work-life balance
  • A diverse, international team with colleagues from more than 45 nationalities
  • A supportive workplace focused on wellbeing, inclusion, and belonging
  • Career development opportunities aligned with your personal goals
  • Helpful, knowledgeable, and collaborative colleagues
  • A workplace where your ideas and feedback are valued
  • Boyum IT committed to responsible business and positive ESG impact

Interested?

Send us your CV in English or Danish.

We review applications and invite candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so there’s no need to wait until the last minute.

You don’t need experience with every technology listed in the advertisement. What matters most is a strong software engineering foundation, practical experience building with AI, and an interest in taking solutions from an idea into reliable everyday use.

We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, identities, and experiences.

title: Generative AI Specialist
description:
• Design, develop, and deploy Generative AI applications using Large Language Models (LLMs).

  • Build and optimize Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines to enable accurate, context-aware responses based on enterprise data.

  • Develop and implement AI agents and multi-agent systems using Agentic AI frameworks.

  • Integrate LLMs with internal systems, APIs, databases, and external tools.

  • Implement prompt engineering techniques, context management, and model fine-tuning when required.

  • Work with vector databases and embedding models to improve information retrieval and semantic search.

  • Develop scalable AI solutions using frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, and LlamaIndex.

  • Evaluate and optimize model performance, accuracy, latency, and cost.

  • Implement security, access control, data privacy, and responsible AI practices.

  • Collaborate with software engineers, data engineers, and business stakeholders to translate business requirements into AI-driven solutions.

  • Deploy, monitor, and maintain AI applications in production environments.




Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field.

  • 1-5 years of experience in AI/ML, Software Engineering, or a related technical field, with practical experience in Generative AI development.

  • Strong programming skills in Python.

  • Hands-on experience working with Large Language Models (LLMs), such as GPT, Claude, Gemini, or open-source models (Llama, Mistral).

  • Solid experience designing and implementing Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) architectures.

  • Practical experience with embeddings, semantic search, vector databases, and document processing.

  • Hands-on experience developing AI agents and agentic workflows.

  • Familiarity with frameworks such as LangChain, LangGraph, LlamaIndex, AutoGen, or CrewAI.

  • Experience integrating AI models through REST APIs and working with backend technologies.

  • Understanding of prompt engineering, context windows, tokenization, and model evaluation techniques.

  • Knowledge of cloud platforms such as AWS, Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud.

  • Familiarity with Docker, Git, CI/CD, and deploying AI applications is preferred.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with LLM fine-tuning, PEFT, LoRA, or quantization.

  • Experience implementing advanced RAG techniques, including hybrid search, reranking, and query expansion.

  • Knowledge of AI safety, guardrails, hallucination mitigation, and LLM observability.

  • Experience building production-grade multi-agent systems and autonomous workflows.

  • Familiarity with MLOps or LLMOps practices.

Please review the following job description:

Provide timely and efficient completion of client transactions while maintaining accurate records and thorough proper handling of all monies assigned. Deliver superior quality service, identifying and understanding the client’s financial needs. Cross-trained to support sales and service activities, with a particular focus on assisting with outbound calling and supporting Integrated Relationship Management (IRM) activities.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Following is a summary of the essential functions for this job. Other duties may be performed, both major and minor, which are not mentioned below. Specific activities may change from time to time.
1. Provide a distinctive client experience to ensure a consistent service level by engaging clients with smiling, facilitating courteous conversation, conducting both complex and standardized transactions while uncovering needs. Performs more complex transactions with assistance as necessary.
2. Educate clients on digital, self-service solutions including ATMs, Online and Mobile banking to make banking easier and enhance their service experience.
3. Support team sales process by participating in client outreach through outbound calls, checking for client offers, and identifying client needs or opportunities by fulfilling the need or referring the client to the appropriate branch team members or specialist.
4. Understand the importance of Integrated Relationship Management (IRM) to ensure we seamlessly deliver Truist expertise and solutions for our clients’ unique needs.
5. Participate fully in all components of the established Truist Retail Community Bank Leadership Routines.
6. Commit to advancing individual and product knowledge to better serve consumer and business clients by attending sales, service and product knowledge meetings and all applicable training classes and web-based learning.
7. Adhere to internal controls, operational procedures and risk management policies. Stays informed of all changes in policies and procedures to ensure compliance with current guidelines.
8. Serve as secondary contact for new account openings and problem resolution, offering applicable products and services to clients and prospects. Handles proportionate volume of work based on branch demands.

QUALIFICATIONS
Required Qualifications:
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
1. High school diploma or equivalent education
2. Two years of teller or cash handling or client service experience
3. Six months of client relationship building or sales experience
4. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including a desire to interact with clients and prospects
5. Ability to master personal computer (PC) keyboard and software skills necessary for branch automation
6. Ability to multi-task under time constraints
7. Demonstrated proficiency in basic computer applications, such as Microsoft Office software products
8. Ability to travel to accommodate temporary staffing needs as required to include temporary assignment or locale changes
9. Ability to work weekends and/or extended hours with occasional travel and overnights may be included

Preferred Qualifications:

1. One year of client relationship building or sales experience
2. Knowledge of advanced or complex branch transactions, risk management and loss prevention
3. Experience with sourcing and prospecting for new clients and client relationship building
4. General understanding of bank operations, policies and procedures

title: Guest Care Associate - Hilldale
description:
As a member of the C&S Wholesale Grocers family of companies, SpartanNash is a food solutions company that delivers the ingredients for a better life. A distributor, wholesaler and retailer with a global supply chain network, SpartanNash distributes grocery and household goods, including fresh produce and the Our Family® portfolio of products, to locations in all 50 states.

Our braggingly happy team members — ranging from bakery managers to order selectors; from IT developers to vice presidents of finance; from HR Business Partners to export specialists — create braggingly happy customers spanning national accounts, independent and chain grocers, e-commerce retailers, U.S. military commissaries and exchanges, and the Company’s own brick-and-mortar grocery stores, pharmacies and fuel centers.

Ready to contribute to the success of our food solutions company? Apply now!

Location:

726 N. Midvale Blvd - Madison, Wisconsin 53705

Position Summary:

This role is responsible for providing courteous customer service in person or by telephone; answers incoming calls to the retail store and directs incoming calls to the appropriate department and assist with guest questions in store. Also responsible for operating cash register and/or assisting guests with self-checkouts.

Here's what you’ll do:

  • Provide courteous guest service in person or by telephone; answer incoming calls to the retail store and direct calls to the appropriate department and assist with guest questions in store.

  • Perform/process guest services transactions such as credits, over-rings, refunds, lottery ticket sales, money orders/transfers (Western Union), media related purchases, etc. in accordance with Company policies.

  • Operate cash register to itemize customer purchases and assist guests with self-checkouts; handles a variety of products which may include dry groceries, frozen foods, dairy products, produce, poultry, fish, beef and pork products.

  • Process financial transactions including, but not limited to; cash, checks, credit cards, food stamps, WIC, loyalty cards, gift certificates, rain checks, voids, and coupons; and bag customer purchases.

  • Maintain understanding of current store programs and product locations.

  • Understand use of check-stand equipment (register, self-checkouts) and its efficient operation.

  • Comply with Company policies regarding security, cash handling/cash drawer accounting procedures, product handling (i.e., damaged/spoiled products), the sale of alcohol and tobacco products, etc.

  • Communicate the Company programs (i.e., loyalty program, scans, etc.), in-store specials and coupons to customers, and models high standards of service to achieve a customer oriented store.

  • Maintain a clean and well-stocked department; ensure the department complies with Company safety and sanitation procedures and standards.

  • Notify the department lead or manager of any issues with pricing, cash registers, etc.

  • Follow all PPE and Safety Guidelines

  • Follow all Food Safety and Cleaning Expectations

  • Follow Guest Experience Guidelines

  • May be assigned tasks in other departments based on customer experience need

  • Additional responsibilities may be assigned as needed

Here’s what you’ll need:

  • High school diploma or GED (required)

  • One year of prior retail or related experience preferred.

  • Good verbal communication skills; ability to interact politely and effectively with customers.

  • Good customer service and organizational skills; detail-oriented. Good reading, writing and arithmetic skills are required.

Physical Requirements:

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an associate to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. May be required to lift and/or move up to 30 pounds frequently, and up to 50 pounds occasionally. The associate is required to stand and walk for extended periods of time and may bend, stoop, twist and turn frequently. While performing the duties of this position, the employee is subject to a typical retail store environment (varied temperatures) and is exposed to outside weather conditions. The noise level in the work environment is usually low to moderate. Travel requirements vary by assignment.

We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all individuals, including those with disabilities and Veterans.

title: Incident Manager (CSIRT)
description:
Do you want to be at the forefront of protecting our society against cyber threats? We are looking for an Incident Manager to team up with the most dedicated team of cyber specialists in our Incident Response domain.

About Truesec – A Leading Cybersecurity Company

Since 2005, Truesec has been a native cybersecurity company, driven by one single purpose: Creating safety and sustainability in a digital world by preventing cyber breach and minimizing impact.

Over the years, we’ve earned the trust of organizations worldwide and gained a strong reputation internationally. Our team consists of dedicated specialists covering the entire spectrum of cybersecurity – with capabilities in Predict, Prevent, Protect, Respond, and Recover.

Today, we employ around 440 employees – and as cybercrime grows, we need to grow. To support that goal, we are now looking for an Incident Manager who wants to make a difference in our CSIRT.

CSIRT (Cybersecurity Incident Response Team)

Our Cybersecurity Incident Response Team (CSIRT) manages most of the large cybersecurity incidents in the Nordics. The team consists of dedicated experts in forensics, advanced infrastructure, and incident management, and works tirelessly to solve the most challenging technical situations. Together, we have rescued countless global organizations from cyber attacks and helped them get back to business with minimal impact.

The Role

As a Cyber Incident Manager, you are responsible for coordinating incident engagements from initial response through containment, forensic investigation, recovery, and post-incident activities.

You will work closely with multidisciplinary teams consisting of forensic investigators, recovery specialists, infrastructure experts, legal advisors, and customer stakeholders. At the same time, you will act as a trusted advisor to customer representatives throughout the incident lifecycle.

Your focus will be on driving progress, aligning priorities, coordinating stakeholders, and ensuring that response and recovery activities move forward efficiently. You will gradually be taking on increasing responsibility as you develop your leadership, stakeholder management, customer advisory, and crisis coordination capabilities.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead and coordinate cybersecurity incident response engagements.
  • Act as a primary point of contact for customers and stakeholders during incidents.
  • Coordinate cross-functional teams consisting of technical and business specialists.
  • Drive recovery efforts to minimize business disruption and downtime.
  • Provide guidance and recommendations throughout the incident lifecycle.
  • Support customers in strengthening resilience and preparedness after incidents.
  • Contribute to the continuous development of Truesec incident response capabilities and methodologies.

Your Potential Background

We believe you have a background in cyber security, IT operations, managed services, consulting, technical account management, service delivery, project coordination, or a similar field.

You enjoy collaborating with both technical specialists and business stakeholders, bringing structure to challenging situations and helping teams to prioritize the work toward a common goal.

Required Skills

  • Understanding how modern IT environments and services are operated and supported.
  • Experience leading major incidents, service disruptions, or crisis situations.
  • Experience advising senior leadership and executive stakeholders.
  • Ability to build trusted relationships with technical specialists and business stakeholders.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and a pragmatic mindset.
  • Professional proficiency in English and Danish, both written and spoken.

Meritorious Experience

title: LVN
description:
Description
Provide your personal attention and kindness, professional insight, and a generosity of spirit. Offer expertise and encouragement. Enhance each patient's future-as well as your own.
Connect with your goals and change lives
with Fresenius Medical Care North America.

Here, we make connections that empower patients, their families, and our team members. As the global leader in dialysis healthcare, we form bonds that enable the best possible outcomes and professional satisfaction. While our extensive organization continues to grow, so do opportunities for our professionals to learn, grow, and advance.

Why Join the Fresenius Team?

Passion. Dedication. Knowledge. Motivation. Experience. These are the impressive qualities you'll find in the Fresenius Leadership Team. Our strength in the North American market and extensive global network provide our employees with the best of both worlds-the friendliness of a local organization and the stability of a worldwide organization-for diverse experiences and challenging career opportunities. When you join the Fresenius Medical Care team, you'll be welcomed into a company that is built on the philosophy that our employees are our most important asset. Our career advantages include the following:

  • Fresenius Medical Care is the nation's largest provider of renal care, meeting the needs of more than 135,000 patients at 1,800 clinics throughout the country.
  • Our well-established, trusted organization fosters a spirit of camaraderie, emphasizing friendly collaboration, professional support, and career development.
  • Superior training, UltraCare® quality control, and certification procedures ensure your potential to succeed and advance as a professional.
  • Competitive compensation and exceptional benefits.
  • Outstanding tuition reimbursement program.
  • Recognized among Fortune's World's Most Admired Companies in 2011.
  • National Safety Award from CNA insurance companies for 11 consecutive years.
  • Opportunities to give back by participating in philanthropy and community outreach programs.

PURPOSE AND SCOPE:

Supports FMCNA's mission, vision, core values and customer service philosophy. Adheres to the FMCNA Compliance Program, including following all regulatory and division/company policy requirements.

Functions as part of the hemodialysis health care team in providing safe and effective dialysis therapy for assigned patients under the direct supervision of a registered nurse. Participates in the implementation and evaluation of patient care. Responsible for reporting and documenting all new or unusual incidents, information, complaints, or problems to the supervisor. Promotes and assists in the maintenance of a safe and clean work environment."

DUTIES / ACTIVITIES:

CUSTOMER SERVICE:

  • Responsible for driving the FMCNA culture through values and customer service standards.
  • Accountable for outstanding customer service to all external and internal customers.
  • Develops and maintains effective relationships through effective and timely communication.
  • Takes initiative and action to respond, resolve and follow up regarding customer service issues with all customers in a timely manner.

PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES AND DUTIES:

Patient Related:

  • Provide direct patient care for assigned patient(s).
  • Perform all technical aspects of dialysis procedures for assigned patients as prescribed. Administer and monitor treatments in accordance with current treatment plan or as directed by the supervisor.
  • Monitor and document dialysis treatment parameters on dialysis flow sheets. Document other information related to the care of the patient in the individual patient record.
  • Responsible for reporting any significant information, change in patient condition, or equipment problems to the supervisor.
  • Assist in developing and following the teaching plan to educate the patient and family regarding end stage renal disease, dialysis therapy, diet and medications.
  • Assist with all emergency operational procedures.
  • Administer intravenous medication in accordance with physician orders and state nurse practice laws.
  • Perform and document pre, interim, and post treatment review of patient condition.
  • Initiate basic CPR measures in the event of cardiac and/or pulmonary arrest, and respond to emergency situations related to dialysis treatment.

Technical:

  • Safely operate all dialysis related equipment according to the proper procedures.
  • Provide minor troubleshooting when necessary.
  • Ensure a clean, safe and sanitary environment in the dialysis facility treatment area.
  • Ensure all blood spills are immediately addressed according to FMCNA Bloodborne Pathogen Control Policies.
  • Operate all emergency equipment effectively in accordance to the standard operation procedures.

Staff Related:

  • Participate in staff meetings as scheduled.
  • Assist in short term and long term patient care plan meetings.
  • Acquire information and knowledge in current practice related to dialysis principals and technique by participating in scheduled in-service classes.
  • Act as a resource person for other staff members. Assist with the coordination of the care plan with Physician, Dietitian and Social Worker.
  • Other duties as assigned.
PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORKING CONDITIONS:
The physical demands and work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Day to day work includes desk and personal computer work and interaction with patients, facility, staff and physicians. The position provides direct patient care that regularly involves heavy lifting and moving of patients, and assisting with ambulation. Equipment aids and/or coworkers may provide assistance. This position requires frequent, prolonged periods of standing and the employee must be able to bend over. The employee may occasionally be required to move, with assistance, machines and equipment weighing up to 200lbs., and may lift chemical water solutions of up to 30lbs., up as high as 5 feet. The position requires travel between assigned facilities and various locations within the community. Travel to regional, Business Unit and Corporate meetings may be required.
The work environment is characteristic of a health care facility with air temperature control and moderate noises levels. May be exposed to infectious and contagious diseases/materials.
EDUCATION:
  • Graduate of an accredited School of Practical Nursing (LPN, LVN)
  • Current appropriate State licensure.
EXPERIENCE AND REQUIRED SKILLS:
  • One year medical-surgical nursing experience preferred.
  • Hemodialysis experience preferred but not required.
  • ICU experience preferred but not required.

title: Facilities Services Technician
description:
Position Overview

The Facilities Services Technician is responsible for developing, coordinating, and managing facility service and preventive maintenance programs across Houchens retail locations.

This position manages recurring and multi-location facility programs designed to improve store conditions, extend asset life, reduce reactive maintenance, and provide consistent service across the organization.

Programs may include HVAC filter replacement, lighting maintenance, high dusting and cleaning, floor care programs, pressure washing, roof and gutter maintenance, inspections, and other preventive facility services.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop and manage preventive maintenance and recurring facility service programs across Houchens retail locations.
  • Coordinate program schedules, store participation, vendor assignments, and service frequencies.
  • Develop scopes of work and service standards for multi-location facility programs.
  • Solicit proposals, compare pricing, and assist with vendor selection and contract negotiations.
  • Coordinate program rollouts with store operations, vendors, and Facilities.
  • Track completion of scheduled services and ensure required documentation is maintained.
  • Monitor vendor performance, workmanship, response, and compliance with established scopes and service standards.
  • Review invoices and validate completed work against contracted pricing and scope.
  • Track program spending against established budgets and identify cost-saving opportunities.
  • Analyze service history and facility needs to determine appropriate preventive maintenance frequencies.
  • Identify opportunities to consolidate services, standardize specifications, and leverage Houchens’ scale across the retail portfolio.
  • Conduct site visits and quality inspections as needed to verify program performance.
  • Maintain program calendars, vendor information, service records, contracts, pricing, and performance reporting.
  • Support the Director of Facilities with development of new facility programs and continuous improvement initiatives.

Typical Programs

Examples of programs managed by this position may include:

  • HVAC filter replacement
  • Interior and exterior lighting
  • High dusting and specialty cleaning
  • Floor cleaning, refinishing, and maintenance
  • Pressure washing
  • Roof and gutter inspections/cleaning
  • Door and storefront preventive maintenance
  • Parking lot sweeping and cleaning
  • Building and equipment inspections
  • Other scheduled preventive maintenance and facility service programs

Qualifications

  • 3+ years of project management, facilities, construction, property management, vendor management, or related experience preferred.
  • Experience coordinating projects or service programs across multiple locations preferred.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple programs simultaneously.
  • Strong vendor communication, negotiation, and follow-up skills.
  • Ability to develop scopes of work, evaluate proposals, and manage projects to budget and schedule.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate program and financial records.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel and work order/project management systems.
  • Ability to travel throughout Houchens’ retail footprint as needed.

Definition of Success

Success in this position means preventive maintenance and facility service programs are completed consistently, on schedule, within budget, and to established quality standards—helping Houchens reduce reactive repairs, extend asset life, and maintain clean, safe, well-maintained retail locations.

.

  • Valid driver licence.
  • Experience with Permit to Work systems, electrical isolations, JHA/JSA and safe systems of work.
  • • HV, QMI, cathodic protection, PLC, analyzer or specialist equipment capability.

You bring your skills and experience to Shell and in return you work with talented, committed people on one of the most important challenges facing our planet. You’ll have the opportunity to develop the skills you need to grow in an environment where we value honesty, integrity, and respect for one another. You’ll be able to balance your priorities as you become the best version of yourself.

  • Perform at your best with a competitive starting salary and annual performance-related salary increase – our pay and benefits packages are considered to be among the best in the world.
  • Take advantage of paid parental leave, including for non-birthing parents.
  • Join an organisation working to become one of the most diverse and inclusive in the world. We strongly encourage applicants of all genders, ages, ethnicities, cultures, abilities, sexual orientation, and life experiences to apply.

We'd like you to know that Shell has a bold goal: to become one of the world’s most diverse and inclusive companies. You can get to know more about how we're working towards that goal, click here.


Shell in Australia

Shell has operated in Australia since 1901. From operating Australia’s first oil refinery, which was central to meeting Australia’s fuel needs, to fuelling the first Qantas commercial flight in the 1920s, to playing a foundation role in building some of Australia’s largest and most innovative natural resource developments.

Throughout this 125-year relationship the needs of our customers and the nation have changed and we have continued transforming our portfolio to meet these needs. Today, we are a leading natural gas producer and are playing our part in the transition to a low-carbon future by investing in the power sector, renewable energy sources and carbon abatement activities.

Shell has a significant Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG) business in Australia that makes a valuable contribution to today’s energy supply. This integrated gas portfolio includes our two Shell-operated gas production and liquefaction businesses, Shell QGC in Queensland and Prelude Floating LNG offshore in Western Australia, and our joint venture interests in Gorgon and North West Shelf in Western Australia and Arrow Energy in Queensland.


Today, Shell’s portfolio in Australia also includes zero- and low-carbon energy businesses such as commercial and industrial retailer, Shell Energy carbon farming specialist, Select Carbon the 120MW Gangarri solar development; residential energy retailer, Powershop Australia a 49% stake in WestWind Australia a 50% share of Kondinin Energy and several grid-scale Battery Energy Storage Solutions projects. title: Project Manager
description:
This position is for a Senior Project Manager (PM3) to assist the State of Michigan Project Management Office supporting Michigan Department of Corrections with high-priority projects.
This role, as part of the DTMB Enterprise Portfolio Management Office (EPMO), works closely with DTMB Agency Services technical teams as well as with agency executives/stakeholders in the delivery of various projects for Michigan Department of Corrections.
The Project Manager will lead a variety of initiatives throughout the year. Projects may include, but are not limited to, technology implementations, organizational initiatives, procurement efforts, and RFP-driven projects within both Agile and traditional project delivery environments. The ideal candidate will have a strong project management background, with demonstrated success leading large-scale, complex projects within government or other public sector organizations.
The candidate must be comfortable working in a fast paced, multi-vendor deployment supporting a hybrid workforce (combination of on-site and remote work) at all levels of the organization.
Applicants should possess exceptional communication and follow up skills along with significant experience in formal IT project management.

Job Duties

  • Utilize the State of Michigan’s Project Portfolio Management Tool (Clarity) to prepare project schedules, assign resources and manage budgets.
  • Prepare information for presentations geared to various audiences ranging from executives, managers and project team members.
  • Accountable for monitoring, controlling, and communicating project progress by actively managing the cost, schedule, scope, resources, quality, and risks.
  • Accountable and responsible for clear, timely, and accurate communications with stakeholders, particularly the project sponsors, project team members, program managers, and DTMB management, on the status of the project, using appropriate communication methods.
  • Responsible for providing leadership and fostering collaborative participation between the technical and business teams by obtaining consensus and gaining commitment.
  • Responsible for managing and communication of interfaces related to other agencies.
  • Responsible for ensuring the project adheres to the State of Michigan’s methodologies, including appropriate and timely transitions through the stages and phases of the project lifecycle.
  • Responsible for facilitating and enforcing the Change Management process (Change Requests) when the project deviates from the approved scope, schedule, or budget. This includes ensuring all Change Requests have appropriate approval before action is taken or information is updated.
  • Responsible for understanding the project benefits and the impact of change requests to the benefits business cases. Responsible for ensuring related project artifacts are updated accordingly.
  • Responsible for reviewing and understanding vendor contracts to actively manage the vendor deliverables and adherence to the vendor deliverable approval procedure.
  • Facilitates interactions among stakeholders by clarifying the expectations of all participants and ensuring all deliverables are assigned, reviewed, and completed.



Requirements

8+ years:
  • Experience as a Project Manager.
  • Experience managing projects with budgets greater than $20 million.
  • Experience managing IT projects within a large, complex enterprise environment.
  • Experience managing vendors and/or third-party solution providers.
Demonstrated leadership, communication, stakeholder management, and organizational skills.
Experience leading multiple concurrent projects and driving work to successful completion with minimal supervision.
Experience handling variety of stakeholders and system/ business owners from other departments.
Experience managing multi-vendor environment in a government environment.
Experience providing project management services for IT Projects involving Commercial Off the Shelf Technology (COTS).
Oversee technical teams with system architecture and integration across SaaS solutions.

title: Solicitor Apprenticeship Programme 2027
description:
Practice Group / Department:

Early Careers Recruitment

Job Description


We're Norton Rose Fulbright - a global law firm with over 50 offices and 7,000 employees worldwide. We provide the world’s preeminent corporations and financial institutions with a full business law service.


As well as the relevant skills and experience, we're looking for people who are innovative, commercial and value the work that they do. We celebrate multiple approaches and points of view and believe diversity drives innovation, so we're building a culture where difference is valued.


Have you thought about law? Are you worried about the costs of university or put off by how competitive it is to obtain a job as a trainee solicitor? Perhaps you are simply keen to get into the world of work and start building a career. If so, Norton Rose Fulbright's Apprenticeship Programme might be for you.

We believe that everyone should have the opportunity to develop to their full potential, which is why we have launched our Apprenticeship Programme to offer an additional route to qualifying as a solicitor. Our apprentices will work alongside and learn from some of the brightest minds in their field, helping to solve some of our clients' most complex legal and business problems while learning the academic and practical skills needed to excel as a lawyer. They will receive a high standard of training from us while studying one day per week. In this programme, you will spend the first 4 years rotating around our key practice groups - Corporate, Disputes and Banking - every 12 months. These rotations will also include Compliance and General Counsel. For your final 2 years, you will mirror a trainee rotation of 4 x 6 month rotations including the opportunity to go on international secondment.

We have up to four vacancies for talented individuals to join our Solicitor Apprenticeship Programme starting in September 2027. We are looking for lawyers of the future - enterprising, digitally minded individuals with the intellectual curiosity and aptitude needed to thrive in our legal business.

This Apprenticeship Programme application window is open everyone who has completed their A-Levels, or final school year leavers who are completing their A-Levels in 2027, and will take place over six years. Applicants should not have completed a university degree and should have the right to work in the UK.

On successful completion of the Programme, our apprentices will have achieved a LLB (Hons) Law and Legal Practice degree and a Level 7 Apprenticeship, qualifying as solicitors. The starting salary will be £30,000, and will increase year on year commensurate with a graduate trainee solicitor salary by the fifth year. All study fees will be paid by Norton Rose Fulbright. Securing a place on this programme is subject to a successful application, psychometric testing, a pre-recorded video interview and assessment day – support will be provided by our early careers team to guide you through this process.

To be considered we require you to have obtained and be on track to achieving AAB at A-Level (or equivalent, i.e. BTEC), however we understand that a successful team only thrives with a diverse range of skills, therefore we are also interested to hear about your strengths and motivations, as well as your extra-curricular achievements. Be assured that we run a fair and contextualised recruitment programme, therefore any mitigating circumstances will also be taken into consideration. For more information on contextualised recruitment please click here.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

To attract the best people, we strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone can bring their whole selves to work, have a sense of belonging, and realize their full career potential.


Our new enabled work model allows our people to have more flexibility in the way they choose to work from both the office and a remote location, while continuing to deliver the highest standards of service. We offer a range of family friendly and inclusive employment policies and provide access to programmes and services aimed at nurturing our people’s health and overall wellbeing. We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer and encourage applications from individuals who can complement our existing teams. We strive to create an inclusive and accessible recruitment process for all candidates. title: CONUS Deployable - Electronic Flight Bag (EFB) Program Manager (USAF)
description:
Company Overview
DelMar Aerospace Corporation in Las Vegas, NV, is looking for talented personnel who can tackle tough challenges supporting manned and unmanned systems.
People are central to our business: we invest heavily to ensure our current and future employees are afforded every opportunity to enhance their skills, knowledge, and abilities. Take the next step in your career by applying for a position at DelMar Aerospace today!
Job Summary
This position manages the Wing and Operations Group EFB program at various CONUS USAF Bomber Bases: the mobile devices, stand-alone computers, mobile device management software and electronic flight publications that B-52H or B-1B bmber aircrew fly with. Aircrew cannot fly without a current EFB, and out-of-date publications carry safety-of-flight consequences, so the work combines hands-on device administration with disciplined implementation of changing higher-headquarters security requirements.
Responsibilities and Duties
  • Manage Wing and Operations Group EFB program in accordance with AFGSCI 11-270 and Baseline Configuration announcements.
  • Serve as the primary Wing EFB Program Manager and liaison to the AFGSC EFB Program Manager (AFGSC/A3TV); maintain Wing and squadron EFB Manager appointment letters and submit them to the AFGSC/A3T EFB Workflow organizational mailbox.
  • Perform the maintenance, upgrade, patching and restoration functions that cannot be handled at squadron level, holding the administrative passcode for the mobile device management (MDM) console, ForeFlight administrator access and local administrator rights on Exclusive Use Stand-Alone (EUSA) computers.
  • Administer EFB devices in BlackBerry Unified Endpoint Management (BBUEM) or the future designated MDM: configure, issue, track, reset and update devices; add and remove user accounts; track lost or stolen devices; and verify unit compliance through device audits.
  • Coordinate with the Stan/Eval Technical Order Distribution Officer, squadron EFB Managers and Stan/Eval representatives so EUSA computers carry current Technical Orders, Currency of Directives, Flight Crew Information Files, Special Interest Items and Flight Information Publications; publish standardized flight publications to Group SharePoint sites and shared drives; and notify aircrew of publication and procedure changes.
  • Manage the ForeFlight administration account, add and delete user accounts, and instruct squadron EFB Managers on configuration for worldwide FLIP use.
  • Manage the commercial internet service that supports EFB connectivity, acting as primary contact with the internet service provider, scheduling repair and service work, and escorting ISP technicians through base facilities as needed.
  • Serve as equipment custodian for all Operations Group EFB equipment; maintain inventory and accountability; distribute and enroll hardware-refresh devices in the AFGSC Device Enrollment Program and MDM before operational use; and decommission obsolete equipment through the Information Technology Equipment Custodian and DRMO.
  • Work with the Resource Advisor to establish sustainment cost and maintain inventory of EUSA computers, battery extenders, charging systems, faraday bags, lithium fire-bag kits, mounts, cases and cables, and report sustainment cost in the annual group budget process.
  • Monitor iOS releases and technology news to anticipate obsolescence, and elevate EFB requirements and concerns to leadership and AFGSC/A3T.
  • Use the Microsoft Teams EFB Program Manager site and SharePoint to track announcements, manage user profiles and assign training to new EFB Managers.
  • Produce the annual EFB Audit Report and EFB Sustainment Report, and support Stan Eval administrative duties as required.
Qualifications and Skills (Minimum)
  • Active SECRET clearance, or a previously held SECRET clearance that expired and was not revoked.
  • Working knowledge of iOS and macOS; two (2) years of IT or device management experience desired.
  • Minimum two (2) years of Microsoft suite experience, with the ability to manage SharePoint and Microsoft Teams applications.
QUALIFICATION WAIVERS
Specific qualifications may be waived by the Government on a case-by-case basis where a candidate has the knowledge and skills to readily support the mission, including device management experience on an MDM platform other than BlackBerry UEM and publications or stan eval experience from another service or mission area. Candidates meeting most of the qualifications listed should apply.

CLEARANCE AND CITIZENSHIP
• U.S. citizenship is required.
• Active SECRET security clearance, or a previously held SECRET clearance that expired and was not revoked. COMPANY MAY FACILITATE QUALIFIED PERSONNEL IN OBTAINING THEIR CLEARANCE.
• Eligibility for access to Restricted Data.
• Work is performed at the SECRET level.

POSITION DETAILS
• Personnel deploy to Air Force Bomber Bases in the United States 3-4 months at a time. NO FOREIGN TRAVEL.
• Periodic Rotations. Normally 90-120 days on /30 days off rotatons....other rotatons feasible. Back-to-back rotations or staggered rotations feasible. Typically, eight hours per day, five days per week with surges when required by the Government. NOTE: Company will work with employees on rotation location and duration.
• Duty hours may shift during exercise support and around holidays but will not exceed nine hours in a day. Changes are coordinated 48 hours in advance.
• Federal holidays are observed, along with AFGSC Family Days..
• Anticipated start on or about Nov/Dec 2026.
• Compensation is negotiable and commensurate with experience. Benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage, paid time off and 401(k).Payment packge depended on rotation schedule.
• Base period plus four one-year option periods.

MULTIPLE DEPLOYED LOCATIONS
Barksdale AFB, LA // Dyess AFB, TX // Ellsworth AFB, SD // Minot AFB, ND // Whitreman AFB, MO
TIMING
If you believe you meet the qualifications and are interested, contact us as soon as possible, and not later than 10 November 2026, to be eligible for a near-term contingent offer. We would also love to hear from you after 10 November 2026.
Contacting us does not obligate you to leave your current position. We do not ask candidates to take any action inconsistent with an agreement with a current employer, or to bring documents, data or customer information with them.
HOW TO APPLY
Apply through this posting or contact us at drodriguez@delmaraero.com or wenderle@delmaraero.com. Inquiries from personnel currently working in squadron scheduling, training or stan eval will be handled confidentially.

Benefits and Perks
When you join the team here at DelMar Aerospace, you will discover true freedom. We believe that one of the key and critical components to personal, professional, and organizational growth is being allowed to fail and learn from those failures. We foster an environment where you can fail so that you can continue to experiment, to push the bar, to discover what has been overlooked all along. Here, you will join a culture that thrives on open collaboration and creativity. You will appreciate our foundation built on the tradition of hard work, integrity, empathy, and accountability.
As a full-time employee, you will enjoy a competitive salary, comprehensive insurance package which includes phenomenal medical, dental, and vision coverage, supplementary life insurance, and the ability to start planning for retirement through our 401k program with company match. In addition, as we grow the opportunities to learn, grow, and develop your strengths will begin to be a focus in your career development. Most importantly, we offer a fun, energetic environment where you will truly feel at home and with family - while reinforcing a strong commitment to maintaining a work-life balance through paid time off and paid holidays.
DelMar Aerospace is an equal opportunity employer and supports diversity in the workplace. Qualified applications will receive consideration for employment without regard to their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran. Our HR teams will reach out to the applicants who met the qualifications and most closely aligned with requirements of the positions.

title: Study Start-Up Coordinator(Clinical Trials)
description:
Study Start-Up Coordinator

Department: Study Start-Up

Job Summary

About Minerva Research Solutions

Minerva Research Solutions is a leading Clinical Trial Management and Support organization dedicated to advancing global healthcare through innovation, operational excellence, and regulatory compliance. We partner with biotech, pharmaceutical, and healthcare organizations to deliver integrated clinical trial support services across the full study lifecycle.

At Minerva, we are committed to maintaining the highest standards of quality, compliance, and efficiency while enabling breakthrough therapies to reach patients faster.

The Study Start-Up Coordinator is responsible for overseeing study startup timelines and coordinating cross-functional activities to ensure all prerequisites for Site Initiation Visits (SIV) and site activation are completed efficiently and on schedule. This role serves as the central coordination point between departments to monitor dependencies, mitigate delays, and ensure operational readiness for successful study activation.

Key Responsibilities

1. Study Start-Up Planning & Coordination

  • Track study startup timelines aligned with project milestones and activation goals.

  • Coordinate cross-functional activities required for study initiation.

  • Ensure all prerequisites for Site Initiation Visits (SIVs) are completed within timelines.

2. Cross-Functional Alignment

  • Coordinate with Regulatory, QA, Marketing, Finance, and Clinical teams to track deliverables and dependencies.

  • Identify bottlenecks impacting startup timelines and escalate risks appropriately.

  • Facilitate communication between departments to maintain alignment on project objectives and deadlines.

3. Timeline & Milestone Tracking

  • Monitor progress against startup timelines using internal tracking tools and dashboards.

  • Maintain accurate startup reports and provide regular status updates to stakeholders.

  • Proactively address delays and support implementation of corrective actions.

4. SIV Readiness & Site Activation

  • Ensure all regulatory, operational, and documentation prerequisites are fulfilled prior to SIV.

  • Confirm site activation requirements are completed and appropriately documented.

  • Support smooth coordination leading to successful site activation.

5. Risk Management

  • Identify potential risks impacting study startup activities and timelines.

  • Collaborate with stakeholders to develop mitigation and contingency strategies.

  • Monitor ongoing startup risks and ensure timely resolution of issues.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Medical Sciences, Life Sciences, Pharmacy, or a related field.

  • MBBS, BDS, or Pharm-D candidates will be preferred.

  • Minimum 1 year of experience in clinical research or study startup coordination.

  • Familiarity with regulatory requirements, clinical trial startup processes, and site activation workflows.

  • Experience working with cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment is preferred.

Key Skills & Competencies

  • Strong project coordination and organizational skills

  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities

  • Ability to manage multiple timelines and priorities effectively

  • Strong problem-solving and proactive risk management capabilities

  • Attention to detail with a quality-focused mindset

  • Proficiency in reporting and startup tracking tools

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • On-time completion of study startup milestones

  • Adherence to SIV and site activation timelines

  • Number of delays/escalations successfully mitigated

  • Effectiveness of cross-functional coordination and communication

  • Accuracy and timeliness of startup reporting and tracking

What You’ll Gain at Minerva Research Solutions

  • Paid annual, medical, and casual leave

title: Charge Review Specialist
description:
As a Charge Review Specialist, you will meticulously review and analyze medical charges and claims to ensure accuracy, compliance, and adherence to billing guidelines. Your role is essential in preventing billing errors, identifying discrepancies, and optimizing revenue for our healthcare organization.


Responsibilities:


Charge Validation:

Review and analyze medical documentation, including patient records, encounter forms, and electronic health records.

Verify the accuracy of CPT, HCPCS, and ICD-10 codes assigned to services and procedures.

Ensure that charges submitted for billing are complete and meet all documentation requirements.


Coding Compliance:

Assess coding compliance with federal and state regulations, as well as payer-specific guidelines.

Identify and rectify any coding errors, discrepancies, or unbundling issues.

Collaborate with coding specialists to resolve coding-related discrepancies.


Charge Accuracy:

Validate the appropriateness of charges for services rendered based on medical records.

Confirm that charges match the services provided and the documentation in the patient's file.

Investigate any undercoding or overcoding issues and take corrective action.


Claim Submission:

Collaborate with billing specialists to ensure that corrected charges are accurately resubmitted.

Prepare and maintain documentation related to charge reviews and corrections.


A/R Follow-up:

Monitor and resolve outstanding claims, communicating effectively with payers, and reconciling payments, while contributing to the clinic's ability to continue providing quality healthcare services to our patients.

title: Associate Director - Tech Product Owner (GLAMS)
description:
About the Team:

Enterprise Systems is the backbone of GSK’s internal operations in Digital & Tech, enabling GSK Global Functions teams such as Finance, Procurement, HR, Legal, Compliance, WREF, CGA and Corporate Secretariat to run seamlessly. This team designs and delivers cutting-edge digital platforms that power critical processes, ensuring efficiency, compliance, and scalability across the enterprise.

Enterprise Systems Management & Business Operations delivers digital solutions that support Enterprise Systems running as a high-performing organisation. This team drives financial discipline, operational rigour and strategic alignment across the ES portfolio that safeguard GSK’s integrity and reputation globally. By joining this team, you’ll help shape systems that support thousands of employees worldwide, driving innovation and reliability in the tools that keep GSK moving forward.

Job Purpose:

The Associate Director - Tech Product Owner (GLAMS) is accountable for maximizing the value of GSK's artwork and packaging digital product portfolio from strategy through operation.

The role translates business strategy, process needs and user outcomes into a clear product vision, roadmap, investment plan and prioritised backlog, while leading discovery, delivery, release, adoption and lifecycle performance. Operating within agreed strategic, financial, architectural and regulatory guardrails, the role balances business value, user experience, technical feasibility, cost, risk, compliance and operational sustainability.

It guides cross-functional teams and partners, owns product decisions and trade-offs, and demonstrates measurable improvement in business performance, adoption, reliability, service effort and user experience.

Key Responsibilities:

· Own the product vision, strategy and outcome-based roadmap for the artwork and packaging portfolio, aligned to business priorities, enterprise technology direction and product lifecycle needs.

· Partner with Business Process Owners, leaders and users to identify unmet needs, simplify processes and translate evidence into product outcomes, epics, features, user stories and clear acceptance criteria.

· Own and continuously refine the product backlog, making transparent priority and release trade-offs based on value, urgency, cost, user impact, risk, compliance, capacity, technical debt and dependencies.

· Lead discovery, planning and delivery with Business Analysts, Architects, Engineers, Testers and partners; clarify decisions quickly, accept completed work against agreed outcomes and maintain coherence between strategy and execution.

· Use AI tooling to accelerate discovery, backlog refinement and requirement drafting, and record where AI-assisted output has been reviewed before acceptance; coach the team in responsible use, including using AI as a coach to challenge assumptions and trade-offs.

· Develop product investment proposals and manage the approved budget, forecasts, supplier costs, benefits, assumptions and total cost of ownership, ensuring investment remains linked to measurable outcomes.

· Define and review measures for adoption, process performance, user experience, stability, service effort, delivery flow and benefit realisation; use insights and feedback to adjust the roadmap and backlog.

· Ensure solutions and changes are secure, integrated, scalable, validated, supportable and compliant with architecture, cyber security, data protection, quality, GxP, change control, records and service-readiness requirements.

· Own product risks, dependencies, technical debt, obsolescence, operational continuity and service performance, documenting decisions and escalating material trade-offs through the appropriate governance forums.

· Lead capability-led vendor and solution evaluations, influence supplier roadmaps and negotiate commercial decisions, and hold internal and external delivery partners accountable for product outcomes and service expectations.

· Drive adoption and continuous improvement by embedding business change, training, onboarding, release communication, documentation and support-model requirements, while identifying responsible opportunities for standardisation, automation, data and AI.

· Coach and develop Senior Product Owners, Product Owners and Product Analysts, providing regular feedback and development support to strengthen product judgement, ownership and delivery capabilities.

Basic Requirements:

Education & Professional Qualifications:

· Bachelor's or Master's degree in a relevant field (e.g., Computer Science, Information Technology, or Engineering), or equivalent experience.

Area of Specialization

· Artwork & Packaging processes, workflows and platforms

· Strategic product leadership and end-to-end product leadership

· Vision, roadmap, investment prioritization, and value realization

· Executive stakeholder engagement, alignment, and governance

· Leadership of product strategy, requirements, backlog, and delivery outcomes

· Driving agile operating models, cross-functional collaboration, and organizational change

· Championing user-centric innovation, adoption, and business transformation

· Ownership of product performance, operational excellence, service resilience, and continuous improvement

· Leadership in enterprise architecture, data strategy, integrations, security, and technology governance

· Influencing and shaping standards, best practices, and product management capabilities across the organization

· Deep understanding of regulated manufacturing, supply chain, quality, and laboratory domains, ensuring compliance-by-design and risk-based decision making

Minimum Level of Job-Related Experience Required

· Typically 7+ years of experience across product management, product ownership, digital transformation or technology delivery in regulated manufacturing, supply chain, quality, laboratory or life-sciences environments.

· Experience in artwork and packaging processes, workflows and platforms.

· Proven accountability for a product or capability from vision, roadmap and investment case through backlog, release, adoption, service performance and lifecycle decisions.

· Hands-on experience translating complex process and user needs into outcomes, epics, features, user stories, acceptance criteria and release priorities.

· Experience leading discovery and iterative delivery in agile or hybrid environments and making timely scope, priority and acceptance decisions with cross-functional teams.

· Exposure to AI tooling used for discovery, refinement or drafting.

· Demonstrated ability to prioritise using business value, user impact, cost, urgency, risk, compliance, operational continuity, capacity and technical dependencies.

· Experience defining product metrics and using adoption, process, user, service, reliability and delivery data to improve performance and evidence benefit realisation.

· Experience developing business cases, managing budgets and forecasts, assessing total cost of ownership and supporting funding and commercial decisions.

· Strong understanding of architecture, integration, cyber security, data protection, GxP validation, quality, change control, service readiness and operational resilience.

· Experience evaluating solutions, managing strategic suppliers and system integrators, and holding partners accountable for delivery, service and lifecycle outcomes.

· Evidence of influencing senior stakeholders, resolving competing priorities and leading global teams through product, process and organisational change.

· Required to make informed product decisions that impact business processes, user experience, and operational performance. This level of experience ensures the Associate Director - Tech Product Owner (GLAMS) can prioritise effectively, guide analysts and delivery teams, and drive compliant, value-centred improvements throughout the Product lifecycle.

Preferred:

· Industry certifications highly desirable (e.g., Agile Methodologies, CPM, Product Ownership, Product Management, ITIL).

description:

Assistant Manager Energy center


Property and Asset Management


GIS 66kV SUBSTATION - OPERATIONS & MAINTENANCE

1. Daily Operations & Switching Activities

Supervise all switching operations, circuit breaker operations, and isolator switching per approved procedures. Monitor voltage, current, power factor (>0.95), and frequency. Coordinate with utility providers for planned switching and execute emergency operations. Maintain operations logbook with complete documentation.

KPI: Zero unauthorized switching; 100% schedule adherence; Equipment uptime >99.5%

2. Safety Protocols & LOTO Procedures

Implement Lockout-Tagout (LOTO) and Permit-to-Work (PTW) systems for all maintenance activities. Conduct safety briefings, ensure proper PPE usage, establish isolation boundaries and earthing. Maintain safety registers and achieve zero electrical accidents.

KPI: Zero safety incidents; 100% LOTO compliance

3. Preventive Maintenance of GIS Equipment

Execute monthly visual inspections and quarterly electrical testing including insulation resistance (>10,000 MΩ), contact resistance (<100 μΩ), and thermal imaging. Perform annual circuit breaker operation checks and protection relay calibration. Maintain maintenance records and trend analysis.

KPI: 100% PM completion; MTBF >15,000 hours

4. SF6 Gas Monitoring & Management

Monitor SF6 gas pressure, purity, and moisture content (<150 ppm). Conduct monthly leak detection and quarterly quality analysis. Coordinate gas top-up with contractors. Maintain environmental compliance documentation.

KPI: SF6 leakage <0.5%/year; Gas purity >98%

5. Protection System Testing

Conduct semi-annual testing of all protection relays, CT/VT accuracy verification, and relay coordination studies. Test trip circuits, interlocking systems, and SCADA interfaces. Document all settings and test results.

KPI: 100% relay functionality; Zero false trips


DG SETS - OPERATIONS & MAINTENANCE


6. DG Operations & Load Management

Ensure automatic changeover within 10 seconds during utility failures. Conduct weekly no-load testing (30 min) and monthly load bank testing (75-80% capacity, 2 hours). Monitor RPM, voltage, frequency, oil pressure, and temperatures. Manage parallel operation and load sharing.

KPI: 99.5% DG availability; 100% successful auto-starts

7. Preventive Maintenance Program

Execute daily checks (fuel, oil, coolant, battery), monthly oil changes (250 hours), quarterly inspections (valve clearance, injectors, turbocharger), and annual overhauls (6000-8000 hours). Maintain service records and running hour logs.

KPI: 100% PM completion; MTBF >500 hours

8. Fuel Management & Quality Control

Maintain 72-hour fuel inventory. Conduct monthly quality testing (density, water content <200 ppm, cetane >48). Monitor consumption (SFC: 0.25-0.28 L/kWh at 75% load). Implement fuel polishing systems. Maintain consumption logs and reconciliation.

KPI: Fuel consumption within ±5% benchmark; Inventory accuracy >98%

9. Emissions & Environmental Compliance

Monitor emissions (NOx <1200 mg/Nm³, SO2 <350 mg/Nm³, CO <800 mg/Nm³). Conduct semi-annual stack testing. Maintain valid Consent to Operate. Control noise levels (<75 dB). Manage hazardous waste disposal through authorized recyclers.

KPI: 100% emission compliance; Valid environmental clearances

10. Vendor Management & Spares Inventory

Manage OEM service contracts ensuring 95% schedule adherence. Coordinate vendor activities and safety compliance. Maintain critical spares inventory for GIS (SF6 gas, relays) and DG (filters, injectors, bearings). Review invoices and conduct performance reviews.

KPI: 95% vendor adherence; Critical spares availability >90%



Reporting:

Being Analytical and Meticulous

Your role will involve coordination with various teams. You will be paying attention to detail and have excellent problem-solving skills. You will be using logic to trouble shoot problems; and assign and monitor maintenance projects. You should have a good knowledge of the working procedures.
